- Windows 11 flyouts and taskbar: the blurred picture behind them was centred instead of aligned to the screen (it stopped short on the right, leaving a strip without blur); it now covers the whole panel.
- Game Hub: the four buttons under the counter (Search, Details, All games, Menu) now act when the finger lifts off them, so they work even when the touch layer swallowed the click.
- Game Hub: the invisible touch targets of the Search, Details and All games buttons overlapped their neighbours (each was 72 px wide, centred left of its button), so taps hit the wrong button; they are now only taller, never wider.
- Game Hub settings: the search box opens Android's own text dialog on a phone, so the keyboard comes up and the matches fill the page.
- Game Hub: a Library button beside All games switches between the phone's own games and the built-in / HTML games library (it shows which one is open); Settings → Game Hub → Library → Select games lists every game with a switch to hide or show it.
- Files: sliding over rows after a long press picks the rows between the first one and the finger, so going back over them lets them go again; the list follows the finger at the edges a notch slower.
